penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: The target segment (productivity-obsessed individuals) is primarily B2C. At $5-15/month per user, the model requires hundreds to thousands of paying consumers to generate meaningful revenue — well above what a solo operator can acquire without paid marketing or viral growth.

rationale: The buyer is a vague 'productivity-obsessed individual' — not a named business role with a budget. Free tools (ActivityWatch, RescueTime free tier, Toggl free) dominate this space, and paying consumers for personal productivity software are rare and high-churn. The core technical requirement — a native agent running on multiple devices (Windows, Mac, mobile) capturing idle/active state and syncing offline activity from wearables — is far beyond what Claude prompts and a landing page can deliver. This is a product that needs a real engineering team and native app development.
solution_plan: This idea is not buildable by a solo non-technical operator using Claude + a landing page. It requires native OS integrations (background processes on Mac/Windows/iOS/Android) to capture application focus and sync with wearables — none of which Claude can generate and deploy without a software engineering team. Even if the data pipeline were solved, the consumer B2C market for paid productivity tracking is crowded and price-sensitive. Pass.
notes: Fails build gates: buildability_with_ai (3 < 6) and operational_autonomy (4 < 7) and buyer_clarity (4 < 6). Total 3.4 is well below validate threshold (5.5). Drop.
